newsitem.title: DENMARK: FOCUS - Superfos has bumper 96, outlook rosy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Superfos has bumper 96, outlook rosy.

text.p: Danish construction company Superfos posted on Thursday bumper profits for 1996 and painted a rosy picture of growth prospects for this year.
It announced a 1996 profit before tax and extraordinary items of 325 million crowns ($50.5 million), 21 percent up on the previous year, on 11.4 percent higher turnover of 5.39 billion crowns.
The result met market expectations of an average 327 million crowns profit and Superfos' own forecast.
Superfos said that it expected 1997 profit before tax and extraordinary items to be 15-20 percent higher than in 1996.
It said there was still major growth potential in the group's core construction, packaging and chemicals units, as stated in a strategic plan unveiled last year.
"The bulk of Superfos' planned growth is expected to come through the acquisition of new companies and activities. The organisational and financial basis for this growth is in place," it said.

One of the three bidders in a protracted battle to take over Danish roadbuilder Phoenix Contractors, Superfos announced on Thursday that it did not intend to raise its offer but had not given up hope of making the acquisition.

Superfos, the favoured bidder of Phoenix's institutional shareholders, had offered 808 million crowns for the company and Phoenix later recommended its shareholders to accept a rival 820 million crown bid from Norway's Rieber & Son.
Earlier Superfos and Colas Danmark signed a letter of intent to jointly acquire Finnish roadbuilder Valtatie Oy from construction group YIY-Yhtyma Oy.

Superfos said its construction division showed the biggest rise in turnover, which was 17 percent up on 1995 and bolstered by takeovers in the United States, where it now had 42 asphalt plants in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Kansas and Oklahoma.
It said its European construction activities were hit by the cold winter and stiff competition but that concrete supply and road servicing activities in Denmark had progressed.
Superfos Chemicals showed a healthy growth rate of 15 percent, with expansion noted in Sweden and Finland, while Superfos Packaging's turnover was static, it said.
It attributed the packaging division's flat sales revenue to lower prices and lost turnover in France due to a major fire at its Besancon plant in 1995.
Superfos raised dividends to 18 crowns per 100 crown share from 15, and said it would split shares into 20 crown units.
The Superfos share closed one crown up at 775, having peaked earlier at 796. --Copenhagen newsroom +45-33969652 ($ = 6.438 Danish Crowns)
